title: add-rag-branch-and-rollback-playbook-with-timebox-simulator
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Adds a new RAG playbook demonstrating branching/rollback semantics with a timebox simulator for tool calls. Useful for authoring resilient multi-tool agents; non-breaking.
description:
Context and motivation: Teams building Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agents frequently need to express conditional branches (forking retrieval/toolflow) and safe rollback semantics when external tools are slow, fail, or return low-confidence responses. This quickstart introduces a compact playbook plus a lightweight timebox simulator to let engineers author branching flows, attach per-branch rollback policies, and validate behavior under latency/failure scenarios.

What this PR adds: 1) playbooks/branch-rollback/README.md - explains the branching model, timebox semantics, and suggested rollout patterns; 2) playbooks/branch-rollback/examples/{node,python} - runnable minimal agent examples that show branching by document-similarity score, fallback to shorter prompts, and automated rollback to a safe summary; 3) tools/timebox-sim - a small simulator service (TS) that can inject latency/failure modes to exercise circuit-breakers and rollbacks; 4) devcontainer and smoke CI job that runs the simulator and example smoke tests in headless mode; 5) docs/snippets/branching-playbook.adoc - a short docsite snippet intended for the RAG patterns gallery.

Checklist: - [x] Quickstart README with step-by-step run instructions and expected outputs - [x] Node + Python example agents (compact) - [x] Timebox simulator with config knobs (latency, error-rate, deterministic seeds) - [x] CI smoke job that runs examples against simulator - [x] Telemetry hooks (example tracing spans + metric names) - [x] Docs snippet ready for docsite inclusion

Guidance for maintainers: The simulator lives under quickstarts/tools/timebox-sim and is intentionally small (single-file TS server using express). It should not be considered production code; it is for local/e2e tests and authoring only. The branching model is implemented in a library-style example (playbooks/branch-rollback/lib) so teams can extract patterns into their own tool bindings. The README outlines trade-offs and recommended rollout (canary + stepwise increase of timebox windows).

Backwards compatibility: Non-breaking. Examples are additive; no runtime or API changes to Redwood runtime are required.

Security and privacy: Examples call a mocked retrieval endpoint and do not include real customer data. Guidance in README recommends using Private deployments or dedicated capacity for sensitive corpora.

Related work: Inspired by ENG-4219 (branching runner research spike) and PM-88 (authoring UX request). Also references the incident runbook from SUP-1023 which motivated clearer rollback semantics for tool calls.

Testing notes: Added smoke tests that start the timebox simulator and run both the Node and Python examples, asserting that rollback occurs within configured time windows and that telemetry spans are emitted. CI initially surfaced a flakiness in the smoke runner which was fixed by increasing simulator deterministic seeding and making the example tests tolerant of ordering on metric emission.
